clue.text: Cupid as worker responsible for strikers leaving the factory?

definitions.meaning: the god of love brings couples together, the job of a romantic go-between

definitions.text: worker responsible for strikers leaving the factory?
definitions.meaning: strikers here are the little sticks you strike to light a fire, so this worker turns them out of a factory

explanation.surface: A god of love is pictured as a factory hand in charge of the workers who walk out on strike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strikers' suggests industrial action, but here it means sticks struck to make a flame, and the person who manufactures them gives the same word as a romantic go-between.
explanation.definitionFit: Cupid unites lovers, as a romantic go-between does; a factory hand making strike-to-light sticks is the literal sense.

clue.text: Mistake with pounds being lost — end of the church?

indicators.note: the pounds are lost, so their letter is dropped from the word for mistake

parts.note: a lapse is a slip or mistake
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling (from Latin libra)

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a costly blunder that loses money is the end of a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being lost' removes L (pounds) from LAPSE.
explanation.definitionFit: The semicircular recess at the east end of a church building has this architectural name.

clue.text: Line to get fish crossing river

indicators.note: the fish goes across the river, so its letters sit either side of the river's letter

parts.note: the cod is a common food fish

explanation.surface: An angler casts a line to catch a fish swimming across a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crossing' sets COD around R.
explanation.definitionFit: A length of string or thin rope is a line.

clue.text: Girl's help accepted by blokes

definitions.note: read as 'girl is', so the definition is just girl and the 's joins it to the wordplay

indicators.note: the help is taken in by the blokes, so it goes inside their word

parts.note: blokes are men, in British slang
aid means help

explanation.surface: A young woman's assistance is gladly accepted by some men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepted by' puts AID inside MEN. The 's of 'Girl's' stands for 'is', linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A maiden is an old word for a young unmarried woman.

clue.text: They knew about Soviet rulers — sort involved with some killing

indicators.note: involved here means tangled up, so the letters of the words that follow are rearranged

explanation.surface: Experts on Soviet leaders are described as a type mixed up in assassinations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' calls for an anagram of SORT and SOME KILLING, all fifteen letters used.
explanation.definitionFit: These were Western analysts who studied the secretive Moscow government during the Cold War, interpreting its leadership politics.

clue.text: Book a member of the university

definitions.meaning: a reading primer or anthology used in schools is called this
in British universities this is an academic rank just below professor

explanation.surface: A book is described as belonging to a university's staff.
explanation.definitionFit: A school primer is one sense; a senior British lecturer ranking just under professor is the other.

clue.text: Contingent not quite intact — soldiers to be brought in

indicators.note: the soldiers are brought into the shortened word, placed inside it
not quite means falling just short, so the final letter of the word for intact is dropped

parts.note: something intact is whole or complete
men is a common crossword word for soldiers

explanation.surface: A military contingent is incomplete, so more troops must be brought in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite' drops the last letter of the word for intact, leaving COMPLET. A complement is the full crew or establishment of a unit.
explanation.definitionFit: A full complement is the whole body of people making up a unit, as a contingent is a group of troops.

clue.text: Writer needing some indication of affection and love

parts.note: a hug shows affection
love is zero in tennis, written as O

explanation.surface: An author is said to need a hug and some love.
explanation.walkthrough: Love is O because 'love' means nil in tennis scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: Victor Hugo was the French novelist behind Les Misérables.

clue.text: Lay one drain anew in the middle of Bude

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go inside the middle letters of the town
the middle of the place name means its inner letters without the first and last
anew means made again in a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone installs a fresh drain in the centre of Bude, a seaside town in Cornwall.
explanation.walkthrough: Bude is a Cornish seaside town. 'anew' gives NORDAINE from the fodder. 'Lay' looks like a verb but is the adjective meaning not of the clergy.
explanation.definitionFit: Lay people are those not ordained as clergy.

clue.text: Member of armed forces, fellow going to Mass, maybe

indicators.note: the fellow goes after the service, so his word is placed second

parts.note: Mass is one example of a church service
a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: A soldier is described as a man who attends Mass.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'maybe' marks Mass as only one kind of church service; 'going to' reads as the fellow attending, but signals the order of the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone serving in the army, navy or air force is a military recruit of this kind.

clue.text: Reversible raised structure

indicators.note: reversible says the word reads the same whichever way round it is taken

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A building or structure is described as one that can be turned back to front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reversible' says the answer reads the same both ways.
explanation.definitionFit: On a ship, the raised deck at the stern is called by this name.

clue.text: Protective layer in shelter, sealed with bit of extra adhesive

indicators.note: the shelter is sealed with the glue and letter, which go inside it

parts.note: a tent is a simple shelter
gum is a glue

indicators.note: a bit of the word extra is its first letter only

explanation.surface: A protective coating is applied inside a shelter, its gaps sealed with a dab of extra glue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bit of' takes only the first letter of 'extra'. The glue and that letter are joined before going into the shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: An integument is a skin, rind or shell covering an organism.

clue.text: Agent doesn't tell the truth giving answers

parts.note: a rep, short for representative, is a sales agent
someone who lies does not tell the truth

explanation.surface: A dishonest agent gives answers that are untrue.
explanation.definitionFit: Responses to questions or letters are synonyms of answers.

clue.text: Dishes away from usual position wrapped in cloths

indicators.note: the word for out of place is wrapped inside the cloths

parts.note: rags are scraps of cloth
something out is not where it usually is

explanation.surface: Plates misplaced from their usual cupboard are wrapped in tea towels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dishes' could suggest plates or crockery, but means cooked dishes: French-style stews.
explanation.definitionFit: Ragouts are stews, served as dishes of meat and vegetables.

clue.text: There's nothing heard that's golden

parts.note: a state in which no sound can be heard, and the proverb says this quiet is golden, worth more than speech

explanation.surface: A remark that nothing audible is precious, echoing an old proverb.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'speech is silver, but ___ is golden' gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The absence of any sound is what the proverb praises as golden.

clue.text: Complaint about home of people in the Bronze Age

definitions.text: of people in the Bronze Age

indicators.note: the complaint goes around the word for at home

parts.note: a moan is a complaint
in means at home

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles about the dwelling places of Bronze Age folk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' meaning at home is a stock crossword equivalence, as in 'staying in'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bronze Age civilisation of ancient Crete, named after King Minos, is described by this adjective.

clue.text: Came across a group of horses in an excited state

parts.note: met means came across or encountered
a stable is a set of racehorses kept by one owner or trainer

explanation.surface: Someone ran into a string of racehorses that were all agitated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Excited state' is physics: an atom or system held in a temporary state above its lowest energy level.
explanation.definitionFit: In physics, a temporarily stable condition above the ground level of energy is called this.

clue.text: Get upset about theologian posing puzzle

indicators.note: the irritating word goes about the degree, which goes inside it

parts.note: to rile is to upset or irritate someone
DD stands for Doctor of Divinity, a theologian's degree

explanation.surface: A theologian asks a puzzling question and gets upset over it.
explanation.walkthrough: DD, Doctor of Divinity, is the usual crossword theologian.
explanation.definitionFit: A riddle is a conundrum or brainteaser.

clue.text: Othello is fine tho 'overcome tragically

indicators.note: tragically suggests things going badly wrong, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Othello is a fine figure, though overcome in tragedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tragically' calls for an anagram of FINE THO OVERCOME; Shakespeare's full title is Othello, the Moor of Venice.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's tragic hero is a North African general serving the Venetian state.

clue.text: Look when female comes in close beside one

indicators.note: the female letter comes into the word for close, going inside it

parts.note: to shut is to close
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: When a woman comes into the room, someone has a look at what is close by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes in' puts F inside SHUT; I follows. A shufti is British slang for a quick look.
explanation.definitionFit: British army slang from Arabic, a shufti means a quick glance.

clue.text: I am left to find meaning

parts.note: I'm is the short form of I am
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: Someone abandoned to puzzle out what something means.
explanation.walkthrough: Port is left on a ship, a familiar crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: The import of a remark is its significance or sense.

clue.text: Money at end of bill produces stress

indicators.note: the money goes at the end of the bill, so its word comes second

parts.note: AC is short for account, which means a bill
a cent is a small coin, so a sum of money

explanation.surface: Seeing the amount at the foot of an invoice causes anxiety.
explanation.walkthrough: AC is short for account, which in Britain also means a bill. 'stress' looks like worry but means emphasis in speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Emphasis placed on a syllable in speech is called an accent.

clue.text: Plant to produce metallic element blowing top

indicators.note: losing one's top, so the first letter of the element is removed

parts.note: gallium is a soft metallic element

explanation.surface: Someone loses their temper trying to make a metal out of a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blowing top' removes the first letter G from GALLIUM. 'Blowing one's top' means losing one's temper.
explanation.definitionFit: The genus that includes onions, garlic and leeks is a group of bulbous plants.

clue.text: Run with broken leg, well pleased to be starting

indicators.note: the self-satisfied word starts the answer, coming before the rest

parts.note: smug means well pleased with oneself

indicators.note: broken means damaged, so the letters of leg are rearranged

explanation.surface: A runner with a broken leg is somehow still pleased to start the race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges LEG into GLE; 'to be starting' puts SMUG first. 'Run' means to smuggle goods, as in gun-running.
explanation.definitionFit: To run contraband is to transport it illegally, as in rum-running.

clue.text: A qualified educationist may be lying

parts.note: a BEd, Bachelor of Education, is a teacher's degree

explanation.surface: A trained teacher might be telling untruths.
explanation.walkthrough: BEd is Bachelor of Education. 'lying' suggests telling untruths, but means lying down in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone abed is lying down in bed, resting.

clue.text: Take a bit of pride in the Open University's work

indicators.note: the letter goes into the university's abbreviation

parts.note: OU is the Open University, a British distance-learning university, and the 's adds an S

indicators.note: a bit of the word pride is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone should be proud of what they produced at the Open University.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bit of' takes P from 'pride'; 'in' puts it inside OU'S. The Open University is a British distance-learning institution.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical or literary composition is called an opus.

clue.text: Support English bank in scotland

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment

explanation.surface: An English bank is said to support a Scottish one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' is not a financial firm but a hillside: brae is Scots for a slope.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scottish dialect, a hillside or steep slope is called a brae.

clue.text: Proper wish formulated by one in church?

indicators.note: formulated means put together in a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A churchgoer is pictured composing a proper prayer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'formulated' calls for an anagram of PROPER WISH. The question mark marks the definition as an example, as not everyone in church is there to pray.
explanation.definitionFit: A person attending a church service is typically praying there.

clue.text: Behind time with others returning

indicators.note: returning means the Latin phrase is read backwards

parts.note: et al, Latin et alii, means and others

explanation.surface: Someone arrives behind schedule when everyone else is coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns ET AL (Latin 'and others') backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Being behind schedule means being tardy.

clue.text: Time to request a little money, new rates from slave-driver

parts.note: to ask is to request

indicators.note: a little of the word money is its first letter
new means made fresh, so the letters of rates are rearranged

explanation.surface: A harsh boss is asked for a little cash and a fresh pay scale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a little' takes M from 'money'; 'new' rearranges RATES into ASTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A harsh boss who works people hard is a slave-driver.
